test_mru_peek.py.rationale: Change B promises that peek() never counts as a use in caches that track use. MRUCache from change A tracks use and evicts the most recently used item. After the merge, peek() on an MRUCache must not change which item it evicts, must not call __missing__, and must not store anything. These tests fail on trees without peek(). They skip on the B-only tree, where MRUCache does not exist.

test_mru_eviction_with_peek.py.rationale: Change A promises that MRUCache evicts the most recently used item, tracking use the way LRUCache does. Change B adds peek(), which reads values without counting as a use. These tests mix plain reads, peeks and size-weighted inserts on an MRUCache. Eviction and popitem order must follow only the real uses. The tests fail on trees without MRUCache. They skip on the A-only tree, where peek() does not exist.

test_cache_classes_invariants.py.rationale: Every tree must keep the exported API resolvable, and ordinary get() must still count as a use in every use-tracking cache that exists. Change A adds an export and change B adds a method next to get(). Neither may break the existing semantics after the merge. Both tests pass on the base.
